thread.title: Boston College prepares for Athens Regional in NCAA baseball tournament
thread.title_full: Boston College prepares for Athens Regional in NCAA baseball tournament

author: Bay State News
title: Boston College prepares for Athens Regional in NCAA baseball tournament
text:
Boston College is set to compete in the Athens Regional of the 2026 NCAA Division I Baseball Tournament, with its first game against Liberty scheduled for Friday, May 29 at Foley Field in Athens, Georgia.
Athens, home to the University of Georgia, presents a different atmosphere compared to Atlanta. The city is known for its alt-rock scene and tourism connected to the Bulldogs’ campus. While Atlanta blends professional sports with college athletics, Athens stands out due to its association with one of the most prominent brands in college sports—the Georgia Bulldogs. The university’s athletic department has won nearly 200 conference championships and recently achieved consecutive national titles under football coach Kirby Smart.
Georgia’s baseball program has historically lagged behind other sports at the university but saw a shift after hiring Wes Johnson as head coach in 2024. Under Johnson’s leadership, Georgia reached its first Super Regional in 16 years and secured both the SEC regular season and tournament titles this year—a program first. Now ranked No. 3 nationally, Georgia will host Boston College (the second seed), Liberty (third seed), and Long Island (fourth seed) in what is considered a highly competitive regional.
“We [started] in January in the bubble [surrounding Alumni Stadium] and felt like we really had a good team,” said head coach Todd Interdonato after his team finished practicing at Harrington Athletics Village on Tuesday. “We felt like we were headed in the right direction [with] momentum from the ACC Tournament [from] last year. Our guys were really focused and committed to basically making the next step and getting to the postseason, and our coaches laid out the plan, or the ‘path,’ as we called it, and our guys were able to execute it throughout the season. Now, we’re here, and we’re reaping the rewards.”
Liberty enters its matchup against Boston College following a strong season that included 41 wins—a high-water mark since joining Conference USA—and prior experience from three recent NCAA tournaments between 2019-2022. “Bradley [LeCroy] coached in South Carolina for a good number of years when I was down there,” explained Interdonato. “So I’m pretty familiar with him and his style… You don’t win 41 games by accident… They’re going to be really good.” Long Island rounds out regional play as champions of their conference tournament after merging LIU Brooklyn’s Division I program with LIU Post’s Division II team.
“Both us and Liberty know that we have a really tough opponent in front of us with each other,” said Interdonato about facing Liberty before possibly playing top-seeded Georgia or Long Island later on.
